context.narrative_job: Introduce the sale-readiness service as a credible business opportunity to a cold viewer, then complete one useful answer inside each net-new avatar-led Short.
context.viewer_before: Earlier versions either jumped into a mechanism before naming the topic, delayed the point, or made the episode carry a missing answer.
context.viewer_after: The viewer knows immediately that an operator can help an owner prepare a business for sale, receives one mechanism or test, and leaves with a bounded conclusion even if every episode route is removed.

data.choice: Lock four exact scripts: The Thirty-Day Map, An Operations Business Wearing a Suit, How You Charge Changes the Job, and Test the Front Door. Each opens with cold-viewer topic and opportunity context, uses the avatar as the conversational guide, and completes a narrow diagnostic, qualification, commercial boundary or channel test. No spoken episode CTA is required. YouTube Related Video may be attached only after the resolved story; LinkedIn ends on the complete professional conclusion.
data.reason: Relationship to EP007 is not enough. A discovery Short earns distribution by being a satisfying first encounter with the channel: recognizable context, useful mechanism and a complete bounded answer. The episode should reward further curiosity with breadth and testing, not repair a contextless opening or withheld payoff.

alternatives.choice: Jump directly into the mechanism to reach the point faster.
alternatives.reason_not_selected: A cold viewer would not know what business or opportunity the mechanism belongs to.

alternatives.choice: Use an incomplete cliffhanger as the required episode handoff.
alternatives.reason_not_selected: It makes the episode supply missing value and weakens the Short as a native discovery object.

alternatives.choice: Repeat one identical series introduction on every Short.
alternatives.reason_not_selected: The topic must be clear, but each Short needs its own conversational angle and narrow promise.

alternatives.choice: Make a spoken episode CTA the climax.
alternatives.reason_not_selected: Routing is additive distribution metadata; it is not the story's conclusion.

reuse.applies_when: Developing an OE companion Short intended both to stand alone and to create informed curiosity about a long-form episode or the channel.
reuse.avoid_when: Producing a pre-launch trailer whose explicitly approved job is an information gap, or treating these exact titles, phrasing, duration or visual treatment as a universal template.

nuance.editorial: Standalone does not mean compressing the whole episode. It means completing the narrow promise made by this Short while leaving adjacent questions honestly open.
nuance.authority: The host may say what service can be built and how to begin. Demand, pricing, channel behavior, legal status and sale outcomes remain bounded unknowns unless separately evidenced.
nuance.avatar: The presenter carries the opening context, reasoning and conclusion. Evidence, diagrams and demonstrations support after the subject is clear; they do not replace the conversation.
nuance.platform: YouTube may attach native Related Video after the conclusion. LinkedIn retains the same complete core and no spoken YouTube CTA.
nuance.false_inference: An owner-approved script is not claim clearance, a performed avatar take, a validated customer service, measured audience demand or publication approval.

data.approval_boundary: Locks the four editorial titles, exact spoken scripts and standalone editorial contract. Final platform metadata, claim-linked Content OS clearance, legal review, visuals, narration, avatar generation, caption timing, phone playback, render, release, publication and provider spend remain separately gated.

evidence.locator: ordered owner direction, exact final approval and bounded interpretation
machine-readable four-script exact-copy lock and standalone contract
owner-readable exact spoken scripts and approval boundary
